tables.title: Surfaced contradictions judged
rows: MRI interpretation disagrees on knee tears

The claims are genuinely inconsistent: one source reports objective MRI findings of horizontal tears in both knees, while another source interpreting the same MRIs says there was no recent traumatic injury or internal derangement. A meniscal tear is a form of internal derangement, so these are not merely different phrasings or compatible observations; they present a real dispute about what the MRIs showed.

The quoted statements are not a clear factual conflict. A "truck" can be a lay description of a Metro-North utility vehicle, so the doctor’s note is compatible with the intake/field-note descriptions rather than truly contradictory.

The claims present a real conflict: one source describes the 2023-08-08 MRI/DTI as abnormal and supportive of traumatic brain injury, while another says the same study shows no traumatic injury and is within normal limits. Those are directly incompatible interpretations of the same imaging, so this is a genuine contradiction worth flagging.

The cited descriptions are materially inconsistent about the crash mechanism: one version says the Metro-North vehicle merged into the client’s lane and struck him, while another says the client’s own vehicle struck the other vehicle as both merged. Those are not compatible ways of describing the same impact direction, so this is a real contradiction worth flagging.

The claims are genuinely inconsistent: the intake paperwork says the plaintiff denied prior work-related injuries and prior injury history, while the file also contains a 2011 left ankle/foot X-ray showing an avulsion fracture of the anterior talus. Those are not compatible facts, and the X-ray is direct evidence of a prior ankle injury that could contradict the denial.

The quoted statements are directly inconsistent on work capacity: the 2024 record says he was "totally disabled from his usual occupation," while the 2026 opinion says he is "able to work and perform activities of daily living without restrictions." A lawyer would likely treat this as a real impeachment issue because it reflects a materially different assessment of disability and employability.

These claims directly conflict: one source says the client "has not been discharged by anyone," while the emergency department record says the client was "Discharged home the same day" on 04/24/2023. A lawyer would likely view this as a real impeachment issue about discharge status and timing.

The cited items are not a clean contradiction. One note says the 22 scene photos had not yet been obtained; a later email says the sender had 22 photos on his phone and could send them, which is a compatible later update rather than a direct conflict. The separate document about plaintiff possessing 22 color-copied photos is also not necessarily the same thing as the scene photos referenced in the note.
Incident report was already in file

The claims directly conflict: one source says the Metro-North Railroad Incident Report was annexed to the discovery response, while a later email says the incident report had still not been produced and did not appear in the response. These are not compatible facts or a mere paraphrase, so this is a real contradiction.

The statements are not a real conflict. The first says coverage information would be provided separately, and the later email actually provides the bodily injury limits. That is a later update/fulfillment, not an inconsistent statement.
Police report said missing despite annexed copy

The claims are in real tension: one source says a copy of the Police Accident Report was annexed, while the later note says there is no police accident report in the file. A lawyer could view that as a genuine inconsistency about whether the report was present in the file/discovery materials, not merely a paraphrase or compatible detail.
Earlier note says no report obtained

The statements are not necessarily contradictory: the 2023-05-23 note says no police accident report had been obtained at that time, while the discovery response says a copy of the report was annexed, which could have happened later. Without proof the report was already available when the note was written, this is a chronological update rather than a real conflict.
